content.text: Spring MVC is a framework used to build web applications. It separates an application into three interconnected components:

items: Model: Represents the data or business logic.
View: Displays the data.
Controller: Handles user input, processes it, and returns the view.

content.text: A collection of dependencies that make it easier to develop web applications with Spring Boot. It includes Spring MVC, Tomcat (embedded container), and other web-related configurations.
A lightweight web container that comes bundled with Spring Boot, eliminating the need for an external server.

items: HTTP Request: When the Tomcat server receives an HTTP request, it forwards it to the DispatcherServlet.
DispatcherServlet: It consults the HandlerMapping to find which controller method matches the request’s URI (endpoint).
Controller: The selected controller method processes the request and may call services or interact with the database (via DAOs, for example).
Building the Response: After processing, the controller prepares the response, often involving data serialization (e.g., to JSON).
ViewResolver: If the response requires a view (e.g., HTML), the DispatcherServlet may consult a ViewResolver to render the appropriate view (this isn’t typically needed for APIs).
Returning the Response: The DispatcherServlet returns the response back to the Tomcat server, which forwards it to the client (e.g., the frontend or Postman).
Lifecycle Repeat: The cycle begins again with each new HTTP request.

sections.heading: Converting IRS Application to a Web Application

subsections.heading: Create a Spring Boot Project Using Spring Initializr

items: Visit the Spring Initializr website.
Choose Maven Project and Spring Boot 2.0.1 version.
Select Web and JPA dependencies (to work with MySQL and Spring MVC).
Click Generate Project and download the zip.

subsections.heading: Set Up Project in STS (Spring Tool Suite)

items: Extract the zip file.
Open STS and import the project:
Check the project structure to ensure everything is in place.

subsections.heading: Create Java Files for Business Logic and Entity Layer

items: User Entity: Reuse the existing UserEntity, UserIdAlreadyPresentException, and UserRepository from the previous demo.
User Model: Implement the User.java model with the necessary fields (e.g., userId, name, email) and validation annotations.

content.text: Create the RegistrationService.java to handle the business logic of user registration.
This controller will manage the home page (landing page).
Handles user registration, including form validation and invoking the registration service.
In the src/main/resources/application.properties file, add the following properties:

content.code:
server.port=4343
server.servlet.context-path=/InfyGoBoot
spring.mvc.view.prefix=/WEB-INF/pages/
spring.mvc.view.suffix=.jsp
spring.datasource.url=jdbc:mysql://localhost:3306/db_irs
spring.datasource.username=root
spring.datasource.password=root

items: Static Resources: Copy your existing css, js, and image files into the src/main/resources/static folder.
JSP Files: Copy the .jsp files (infyGoHome.jsp, register.jsp, header.jsp, footer.jsp) into the src/main/webapp/WEB-INF/pages folder.

content.text: Add the necessary dependencies for JSP processing:

items: Right-click the project and choose Run As > Spring Boot App.
Open your browser and navigate to: http://localhost:4343/InfyGoBoot
The infyGoHome.jsp will be displayed. Clicking on SIGN UP will show the registration page (register.jsp).

Spring Boot Auto-Configuration: Spring Boot auto-configures components such as the embedded Tomcat container, view resolvers, and Spring MVC, which means no need for web.xml or dispatcher-servlet.xml.
Embedded Tomcat: Spring Boot includes an embedded Tomcat server, so you don’t need an external application server. You can configure the port and context path in application.properties.
Deployment to External Container: To deploy to an external Tomcat container, change the scope of the embedded Tomcat dependency to provided in pom.xml.
